question:
A 39-year-old male seeks medical attention for fatigue that has persisted for several weeks. He
discloses a history of body image concerns since his teenage years and is currently attempting weight
loss to improve his appearance in swimwear. He acknowledges episodes of binging and purging.
Physical examination reveals: - Height: 170 cm - Weight: 63.5 kg - BMI: 22 - Blood pressure: 112/72
mm Hg - Heart rate: 92 beats/min Laboratory findings show: | | Patient value | Reference range | | --- |
--- | --- | | Sodium (mEq/liter) | 139 | 136–145 | | Potassium (mEq/liter) | 3.1 | 3.5–5.0 | | Chloride
(mEq/liter) | 90 | 98–106 | | Bicarbonate (mEq/liter) | 40 | 21–30 | Additional findings include elevated
serum pH and increased urinary levels of sodium, potassium, and chloride. Which purging method is
this patient most likely employing? Answer Choices: (A) Nasogastric suctioning (B) Laxative use (C)
Self-induced vomiting (D) Chronic fasting (E) Laxative abuse (F) Diuretic use (G) Use of herbal "detox"
supplements (H) Overhydration with water-loading (I) Excessive exercise (J) Surreptitious use of
antacids
 A. Self-induced vomiting
B. Use of herbal "detox" supplements
C. Laxative use
D. Excessive exercise
E. Chronic fasting
F. Laxative abuse
G. Surreptitious use of antacids
H. Diuretic use
I. Nasogastric suctioning
J. Overhydration with water-loading
